questions.prompt: "Open for extension, closed for modification" — new behavior is added by writing a NEW subclass while existing code stays untouched. Which principle?
options: OCP — Open-Closed Principle
SRP — Single Responsibility
DIP — Dependency Inversion
ISP — Interface Segregation
questions.explain: **OCP**: extend by ADDING code (new subclass/implementation), never by EDITING working code. The drill's exporter example: new formats plug in as new classes.

questions.prompt: `RenderShape(Shape s) { if (s is Circle) ... else if (s is Square) ... }` — every new shape forces editing this method. Which principles are violated, and what is the fix?
options: OCP (and LSP in spirit) — replace type tests with polymorphism: abstract Draw() overridden per shape; RenderShape calls s.Draw() and is closed forever
SRP only — split the if into two methods
DIP only — inject the if-statement
Nothing is wrong — type tests are idiomatic
questions.explain: A function that must know every derivative of its base **violates OCP** (changes whenever a new derivative appears) and abuses the base-class reference (LSP in spirit). Fix = **dynamic binding**: `public abstract void Draw();` per-shape overrides; `RenderShape(Shape s) => s.Draw();`.

questions.prompt: `Resize(Rectangle r)` sets width and asserts height unchanged; passing a `Square` (where setting width also sets height) breaks it. Which principle and why?
options: LSP — the subclass breaks the implied contract clients have with the base class (5×4 became 4×4)
OCP — the method wasn't extended
ISP — the interface is too fat
SRP — Resize does two things
questions.explain: **LSP violation**: clients of Rectangle reasonably assume setting width leaves height alone; Square breaks that. "A model that is self-consistent is not necessarily consistent with all its users." Fix: don't derive mutable Square from mutable Rectangle — both implement `IShape.GetArea()` (immutable), nothing to break.

questions.prompt: Under LSP's Methods Rule, a subtype's overriding method may:
options: WEAKEN preconditions (require less) and STRENGTHEN postconditions (deliver more) — never the reverse
Strengthen preconditions and weaken postconditions
Change the method signature freely
Throw NotSupportedException for unneeded methods
questions.explain: **Signature Rule**: preserve supertype signatures. **Methods Rule**: weaker preconditions, stronger postconditions, invariants maintained — so all reasoning about base-class calls stays valid. Throwing 'not supported' stubs is itself an LSP breach.

questions.prompt: `IMachine { Print; Scan; Fax }` forces BasicPrinter to stub Scan/Fax with NotSupportedException. Diagnose + fix:
options: ISP violated (fat interface) — segregate into IPrinter/IScanner/IFax; the MFP implements all three; the stubs were also an LSP danger
OCP violated — add a fourth method
DIP violated — new the printer inside
SRP violated — printers can't scan
questions.explain: **ISP**: no client should depend on methods it doesn't use. Segregate by client need; multifunction devices COMPOSE interfaces (`OfficeMFP : IPrinter, IScanner, IFax`). The throwing stubs would blow up anywhere an IMachine is expected — Martin notes exactly this LSP hazard in the ISP paper.

questions.prompt: `OrderManager` validates, computes tax, saves to DB, and emails — three teams keep colliding in it. Diagnose + fix:
options: SRP violated (four reasons to change) — split into OrderValidator, TaxCalculator, OrderRepository, CustomerNotifier + an OrderService coordinator
LSP violated — OrderManager needs a base class
OCP violated — make every method virtual
ISP violated — make one big interface
questions.explain: **SRP**: one reason to change per class. Validation rules, tax law, persistence tech and email content are FOUR independent change axes — split them; a thin coordinator orchestrates via their interfaces; team edits stop colliding.

ISP violated — SqlDatabase has too many methods
SRP violated — reports shouldn't query
Nothing wrong — new is required somewhere
questions.explain: **DIP**: depend on abstractions. `ReportService(IDatabase db)` (constructor injection) → swapping SQL→Mongo = a new IDatabase implementation, ReportService unchanged. Note the synergy: **DIP enables OCP** (ReportService is now closed).

questions.prompt: "Add new codec decoders WITHOUT altering the playback engine" + "each decoder subclass can replace another preserving expected behavior" name which two principles?
options: OCP (extension without modification) and LSP (substitutability preserving behavior)
SRP and DIP
ISP and SRP
DIP and ISP
questions.explain: Sentence 1 is the OCP definition; sentence 2 is LSP. Design: `IAudioDecoder.Decode(stream)` (same signature for all — Signature Rule); `PlaybackEngine.Play(IAudioDecoder d)` depends only on the abstraction — closed forever.
